Cairo: Saudi Arabia’s air defences destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered prohibited airspace over the holy city, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Wednesday, as fighting spreads in the Middle East.

The drone, intercepted on Tuesday evening, was the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca after a ballistic missile launch in July 2017, spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a statement, and follows a week of attacks from Iran-aligned Houthi fighters that have drawn Saudi Arabia deeper into the war.

Mecca is home to some of the holiest sites in Islam and the focal point of the annual hajj pilgrimage, and its security was a “red line,” the coalition spokesperson al-Malki said in the statement.

Show Full Article

Houthi officials have denied targeting Mecca.

The attacks on Saudia Arabia have shocked global energy markets roiled by the six-month U.S.-Iran war, which has slowed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to a trickle.

The Houthis have seized control of parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in recent days overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important shipping straits, threatening Saudi Arabia’s oil exports rerouted from the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia issued security alerts for Mecca on Tuesday, but Houthi political bureau member Mohammed al-Farah denied the group had targeted the city, calling the allegation “an outright lie” in comments carried by the Houthi-run SABA news agency.

The Houthis have announced several major attacks on Saudi Arabia over the past week, including attacks on an air base on Monday, which they said were in retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. The air base attack wounded 13 civilians, Saudi-led military coalition officials said.

Saudi Arabia has blamed a separate pro-Iranian movement, based in Iraq, for an attack on Friday that knocked out one of the kingdom’s most important oil transport routes, the East-West Pipeline across the Arabian desert.

The 1,200-km (745-mile) East-West Pipeline linking Saudi Arabia’s Gulf oil fields to the Red Sea has been the kingdom’s principal export route while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has been disrupted by nearly seven months of war, which has killed thousands of people across the region.

Since the pipeline was shut after Friday’s attack, traders say a prolonged closure could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply.

Saudi Arabia has not said when operations might resume.

But U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on Tuesday that crude oil should be flowing through the pipeline within days.

Saudi Arabia has led a coalition battling the Houthis since 2015. The conflict had largely quietened under a ceasefire in recent years, but reignited when the Houthis pushed back forces aligned with the Yemeni government this month.

Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman phoned U.S. President Donald Trump last week seeking military support, which so far has been limited to intelligence aid.

items.title: China insta a los países a frenar las tendencias históricas regresivas
items.author: Mei Mei Chu
items.creator: Mei Mei Chu
items.summary: El ministro de Defensa de China, Dong Jun, instó el miércoles a las naciones a evitar actos provocadores y frenar el resurgimiento de tendencias históricas regresivas, en comentarios que probablemente serán interpretados como una crítica velada a Japón.
items.body:
El ministro de Defensa de China, Dong Jun, instó el miércoles a las naciones a evitar actos provocadores y frenar el resurgimiento de tendencias históricas regresivas, en comentarios que probablemente serán interpretados como una crítica velada a Japón.
Las declaraciones de Dong en el Foro Xiangshan de Pekín sobre seguridad se producen en un momento de fuertes tensiones regionales por Taiwán, reclamado por China, y por la disputada vía marítima del mar de China Meridional, mientras crecen las dudas sobre los compromisos de seguridad tradicionales de Estados Unidos con Asia.
Al advertir que el mundo ha llegado a un “momento delicado”, Dong pidió un enfoque más renovado y equitativo para resolver las tensiones internacionales, aunque ofreció pocos detalles concretos o críticas directas a sus rivales.
“Debemos tener presentes las lecciones de la historia y mantenernos muy vigilantes ante todas las manifestaciones latentes de hegemonía, militarismo y revisionismo histórico”, dijo en su discurso de apertura.
“No debemos hacer la vista gorda ni tolerar ese comportamiento. Movilizando amplias fuerzas de justicia, debemos reprimir el resurgimiento de los residuos del pasado histórico y evitar que aprovechen la situación para causar daño”.
SIN CRÍTICAS DIRECTAS A ESTADOS UNIDOS NI A SUS ALIADOS REGIONALES Tal y como predijeron algunos analistas, Dong evitó las críticas directas a Estados Unidos o a sus aliados regionales, como Japón, y pareció ceñirse estrictamente a las posiciones que China mantiene desde hace tiempo.
“No debemos mostrar indulgencia hacia actos provocadores que buscan secuestrar los intereses generales de los países de la región en beneficio propio o de determinados grupos, y debemos trabajar juntos para contenerlos”, añadió.
Los comentarios llegan una semana antes de que el presidente chino, Xi Jinping, viaje previsiblemente a Estados Unidos para una cumbre con el presidente Donald Trump.
Las relaciones entre China y Japón se deterioraron gravemente el año pasado después de que la primera ministra japonesa, Sanae Takaichi, sugiriera que un hipotético ataque chino contra Taiwán podría desencadenar una respuesta militar japonesa.
Esto llevó a Pekín a advertir en repetidas ocasiones de que Japón estaba tratando de volver a su pasado agresivo.
China considera que Taiwán, gobernado democráticamente, forma parte de su territorio y ha intensificado la presión militar en torno a la isla, lo que incluye la realización periódica de maniobras militares. El Gobierno de Taiwán rechaza las reivindicaciones soberanistas de Pekín.
Alrededor de 2.000 oficiales militares, diplomáticos y académicos de decenas de países participan en el evento de tres días, que se prolongará hasta el jueves.

午後３時のドル／円は、前日ニューヨーク市場終盤とほぼ横ばいの１５５円前半で推移している。原油価格の上昇基調を受けてドル買いが進み、午前の取引では一時１５５円半ばまで上昇した。ただ、日本時間の１７日未明に米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）の結果公表を控え、次第に様子見ムードも広がった。

朝方１５５円前半で推移していたドルは一時、１５５．４９円に上昇。原油価格が高止まりする中、先々のインフレを警戒する動きが強まったとの声があった。足元でレジスタンスとして意識されていた１５５．２０―３０円台を上抜けたことで、トレンドが上昇に転じたとの見方も聞かれた。

１６日付読売新聞は、１７日に見込まれる内閣改造で城内実成長戦略相の続投が有力と報じた。内閣改造でリフレ色が薄まるかが市場の注目の一つだったため、既に続投が報じられている片山さつき財務相と併せ、「留任であれば、市場への影響はなさそうだ」（国内銀の為替ディーラー）との声が聞かれた。

午後の取引では狭い値幅での動きが続いた。ＦＯＭＣの結果公表を控える中で、手掛けにくさも意識された。マネックス証券のチーフ・ＦＸコンサルタント、吉田恒氏はＦＯＭＣについて、「利上げを実施しても、見送った場合でも、特に債券市場や株式市場は荒れる可能性がある」と指摘する。仮に利上げを見送った場合は、「ビハインド・ザ・カーブが意識されて長期金利が急騰するリスクがある」と話す。一方、株式市場は利上げを嫌気して売りが出るのではないか、という。

吉田氏は「特に最近の為替相場は一つの材料で過敏に反応する傾向があるので、イベント後の動きに警戒したい」と話した。

US, Vietnam firms to sign agreements as To Lam travels to New York, documents show

FAST

HANOI, Sept 16 : A string of agreements is expected to be announced next week by U.S. and Vietnamese corporations involving energy, tech, aviation and financial firms as Vietnam's leader To Lam travels to New York, according to officials and two documents reviewed by Reuters.
Commercial agreements, many of which are expected to be non-binding, have been for months part of Vietnam's strategy to mollify Washington as the Trump administration is threatening new tariffs on the export-reliant Southeast Asian nation.
One internal planning note lists 29 agreements that could be announced on September 23 in New York at a business conference to be attended by To Lam. 
U.S. energy firms Murphy Oil and Chevron are expected to announce agreements with state-owned Petrovietnam, while ExxonMobil is slated to announce an accord with Vietnam Refinery and Petrochemical Corporation, the country's second-largest refinery.

In February the refinery signed a non-binding oil supply agreement with Chevron, but no subsequent purchase was announced. Murphy Oil is active in oil and gas explorations in Vietnam, while ExxonMobil operates the country's largest gas field which remains however untapped. 
The agreements are to be announced on To Lam's last day in New York before he travels to Canada for a state visit.
He is expected to speak at the U.N. General Assembly on September 22 and hold meetings with several U.S. corporations, three officials said. His schedule has not yet been officially announced.
His trip is also aimed at making progress on trade talks with the United States, and possibly to agree on a trade deal which has been negotiated for more than a year, two of the officials said.
However, a meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump is not certain, the sources said. Trump's schedule was not yet confirmed, a White House official said on Tuesday.
Vietnam's foreign ministry nor any of the companies cited in this article immediately responded to requests for comment, some out of their business hours.
AVIATION, TECH
The document, which may be subject to changes and does not indicate the content of the planned agreements, also lists several deals involving Vietnam's largest private airline, Vietjet, including with aviation partners and SpaceX.
The company is expected to announce the leasing of as many as 22 planes from four aviation leasing companies, including 17 Boeing 737 jets and five Airbus A321neo, according to a separate document from Vietjet.
The planned contract with SpaceX is for the provision of satellite internet services from Starlink to 120 Vietjet aircraft, according to the Vietjet document.
The airline also plans to sign memoranda of understanding with U.S. jet engine maintenance firms, according to the documents.
The provisional list also includes an unspecified agreement between Meta and Vietnam's ministry of culture, and a separate agreement between U.S. chip giant Qualcomm with Vietnamese telecom firm VNPT. Qualcomm is already active in the rollout of Vietnam's 5G network, while Meta's Facebook is the most popular social media in the Communist-ruled nation.
Visa, Mastercard and Citibank are also expected to announce agreements with financial and hospitality partners in Vietnam, according to the document.

Source: Reuters

items.title: La inflación de Reino Unido se acelera hasta el 3,1%, pero el índice subyacente se mantiene estable
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La inflación británica se aceleró en agosto hasta alcanzar un máximo de cinco meses, situándose en el 3,1% frente al 2,9% registrado en julio, revelaron las cifras oficiales un día antes de que se conozca si el Banco de Inglaterra mantiene las tasas de interés sin cambios a pesar del aumento de las presiones sobre los precios.
items.body:
La inflación británica se aceleró en agosto hasta alcanzar un máximo de cinco meses, situándose en el 3,1% frente al 2,9% registrado en julio, revelaron las cifras oficiales un día antes de que se conozca si el Banco de Inglaterra mantiene las tasas de interés sin cambios a pesar del aumento de las presiones sobre los precios.
El aumento de agosto coincidió con la previsión media de los economistas encuestados por Reuters, quienes pronosticaron que la inflación de los precios al consumo se aceleraría debido a un nuevo repunte de los precios de la energía provocado por la reanudación del conflicto en el golfo Pérsico.
El Banco de Inglaterra pronosticó en julio que la inflación interanual se situaría en el 2,8% en agosto.
La libra esterlina cayó ligeramente tras la publicación de las cifras de inflación el miércoles.
A pesar de que la tasa de inflación general ha resultado ser superior a lo que esperaba el banco central, es probable que los dirigentes monetarios presten más atención a los indicadores subyacentes del crecimiento de los precios, que se ven menos afectados de forma inmediata por el repunte de los costos energéticos.
La Oficina Nacional de Estadística (ONS, por sus siglas en inglés) reveló que su indicador de inflación subyacente —que excluye partidas volátiles como los alimentos y los combustibles— se mantuvo en el 2,6% por cuarto mes consecutivo en agosto.
La inflación en el sector de los servicios británico —un indicador que el Banco de Inglaterra (BoE) sigue de cerca, ya que refleja el crecimiento salarial y las presiones inflacionistas a largo plazo— también se mantuvo sin cambios en el 3,4%.
Los datos de la ONS publicados el martes mostraron que el crecimiento salarial se mantuvo cerca de su nivel más bajo desde 2020.
Los inversionistas estiman que hay una probabilidad de un 33% de que el Banco de Inglaterra suba las tasas un cuarto de punto el jueves. Sin embargo, se dan por hechas dos subidas antes de que finalice 2026, en un contexto de preocupación por el riesgo de que el repunte de los costos energéticos impulse al alza los precios de forma más generalizada.

items.title: Los aeropuertos españoles de Aena registraron 34,9 millones de pasajeros en agosto
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Unos 34,9 millones de pasajeros pasaron por los aeropuertos españoles de Aena en agosto, un 4,7% más que en el mismo mes del año pasado, según informó el martes el operador aeroportuario.
items.body:
Unos 34,9 millones de pasajeros pasaron por los aeropuertos españoles de Aena (AENA.MC) en agosto, un 4,7% más que en el mismo mes del año pasado, según informó el martes el operador aeroportuario.
El aumento del número de pasajeros pone de relieve la resistencia de España como centro turístico, incluso en un momento en que el sector aéreo mundial se enfrenta a la inestabilidad geopolítica, los retrasos en la entrega de aviones, la escasez de mano de obra y el aumento de los costes operativos, factores que han limitado el crecimiento de la capacidad en otros lugares.
El número de pasajeros en los primeros ocho meses de 2026 alcanzó los 225,5 millones, un 4,1% más que hace un año
El Aeropuerto Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas siguió siendo el más transitado de España, seguido por el Josep Tarradellas Barcelona-El Prat y el de Palma de Mallorca
Todos los aeropuertos gestionados por Aena —46 aeropuertos y dos helipuertos en España, 17 aeropuertos en Brasil, así como el de Luton, en Londres, y el Leeds Bradford— registraron un aumento del 4,7%, hasta alcanzar los 41,4 millones de pasajeros en agosto

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: British defence and engineering group Babcock International reaffirmed its full-year outlook on Wednesday on the back of strong momentum across its marine, nuclear and land businesses amid higher defence spending.
items.body:
British defence and engineering group Babcock International (BAB.L) reaffirmed its full-year outlook on Wednesday on the back of strong momentum across its marine, nuclear and land businesses amid higher defence spending.
Here are some details from its trading update:
The company, which maintains Britain's naval fleet, provides weapons systems and supports nuclear projects, said its performance was supported by strong demand across core defence and nuclear markets
Babcock's update comes amid defence firms reaping benefits of militaries rearming heavily against heightened geopolitical tensions and the Iran war.
The firm which has several contracts with the British military said it was awaiting further details on the government's expanded defence investment after a £15 billion ($20.22 billion) [USN:L1N43205S TEXT:"plan"] was laid out in June in a boost for domestic suppliers.
Analysts per a company-provided poll expect Babcock to log 2027 sales of £5.49 billion and an underlying operating profit of £464 million, up from year ago's £5.19 billion and £293 million, respectively.
Larger rival BAE Systems (BAES.L) in July raised its 2026 profit outlook on soaring defence orders.
($1 = 0.7418 pounds)

items.title: India's NSE to launch IPO amid investor caution over derivatives-fuelled growth
items.author: Jayshree Pyasi, Vivek M, Ankur Banerjee
items.creator: Jayshree Pyasi, Vivek M, Ankur Banerjee
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) will launch its $2.3 billion public offering on Wednesday amid investor caution over capital market firms because of declining derivative trading volumes, which have already impacted the offer price.
items.body:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) will launch its $2.3 billion public offering on Wednesday amid investor caution over capital market firms because of declining derivative trading volumes, which have already impacted the offer price.
The IPO for India's biggest bourse — set to be the country's third-largest ever — will begin with anchor investor bidding from institutional funds and is an offer-for-sale from existing private shareholders with no new capital being raised. Open subscriptions will begin on Thursday and close on September 21.
Investors are being asked to value the world's largest derivatives bourse at a time when its biggest growth engine is slowing down, raising questions about how much of the exchange’s extraordinary derivatives-driven growth can continue.
The NSE shares will be offered in a price band of 1,700 to 1,785 Indian rupees ($17.72 to $18.60), [USN:L4N4521GX TEXT:"valuing"] the company at $46 billion, public filings showed on September 11.
However, that is 15% to 20% lower than the valuation sought in pre-deal roadshows, according to two sources with direct knowledge of the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity, and is 40% lower than what private markets sales of NSE shares in 2024 indicated.
Investors are reluctant to pay higher prices because of [USN:L4N43G0S4 TEXT:"regulatory changes"] that have slowed growth in options trading and an overhaul of [USN:L4N44A0T5 TEXT:"trading rules"] to align Indian markets with global standards. The NSE gains 80% of its revenue from trading of which 60% is options trading and those volumes have dropped 27% from their peak in 2024.
"NSE's high exposure to derivatives is a double-edged sword. Its dominant liquidity pool and scale are clear competitive strengths, but they also make earnings more sensitive to regulatory changes and shifts in trading activity," said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments.
Still, even at this valuation, NSE would be among the top 10 largest listed exchanges globally.
At the lowered offer price, several global institutional investors, including sovereign wealth funds and long-only asset managers, have provided commitments, the two sources with knowledge of the matter said.
That includes Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Singapore's GIC, Fidelity, Carmignac, Norges Bank Investment Management and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), they said.
GIC, Norges, ADIA, Carmignac and Fidelity declined to comment when contacted by Reuters, while queries sent to LIC were not answered.
In a press conference on Saturday, Sriram Krishnan, chief business development officer at NSE, pointed to a disconnect between the offer price and current shareholder expectations.
"Some of the shareholders feel that the NSE's valuation is much more than the valuation at which we are proposing to do the IPO. To them NSE is more [USN:L4N45209D TEXT:"valuable"]. There is some money on the table, possibly."
OPTIONS SLOWDOWN TESTS VALUATION The NSE has seen a bottom-line impact from its reduced derivative trading volumes. The exchange's revenue from operations fell 3.1% in the fiscal year ending March 2026, while profit dropped 15.5%.
According to Bernstein, Indian equity derivatives volumes are entering a phase of normalisation and they forecast growth will slow to about 5% in the fiscal year ending in 2027 due to regulatory measures on options trading.
Still, the NSE's IPO valuation implies a forward earnings multiple of 35 to 38 times FY2028 earnings, higher than the 23 to 31 times earnings global exchange operators Nasdaq, CME Group, Deutsche Börse, HKEX and LSEG currently trade.
"The current pricing is factoring, options trading slowdown due to regulatory tightening and initial teething issues in the new mechanism to determine [USN:L4N4570CO TEXT:"closing prices"]. Perhaps had the IPO launched at any other time, valuation could have been better," said Anubhav Dayal, founder of Hong Kong-headquartered fund manager Soach Global Corporation.
His flagship fund is selling 20% of its NSE holding in the offering.
In the past 15 months, the NSE has launched electricity futures, electronic gold receipts, natural gas futures and incorporated a national coal exchange.
On Saturday, NSE's Krishnan pointed to these efforts as positives that outweigh any short-term concerns around derivative volumes.
"In the longer term, there will be so much diversification of revenue and as a natural consequence people will forget this current focus on index options," he said.
($1 = 95.9500 Indian rupees)

items.title: Malaysia talks to rival airlines as it monitors AirAsia's financial health, sources say
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have both expressed their willingness to expand organically to absorb AirAsia's routes and passengers rather than acquire its whole business, sources said.
items.body:
Advertisement

Asia

Malaysia talks to rival airlines as it monitors AirAsia's financial health, sources say

Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have both expressed their willingness to expand organically to absorb AirAsia's routes and passengers rather than acquire its whole business, sources said. 

AirAsia planes stand on the tarmac at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 in Sepang, Malaysia, on Jan 21, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Hasnoor Hussain)

FAST

KUALA LUMPUR/HONG KONG: Malaysia's government has asked Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air whether they can absorb AirAsia's domestic market share, said two people with knowledge of the matter, as part of what they described as scenario planning while authorities monitor the financial health of Southeast Asia's largest low-cost airline.
Discussions between the government and Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have increased in recent weeks, the people said, amid growing concerns over financial pressures faced by AirAsia.
The airline has been hit by soaring jet fuel costs stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran that surged 66 per cent in the second quarter from the prior quarter to an average of US$183 a barrel. 
The talks, which involve the finance ministry and state-linked airport operator Malaysia Airports Holdings, are part of broader scenario planning around AirAsia's financial strains, the people said.

Other options that have been discussed include the government providing some form of endorsement to bolster the airline's plan to raise fresh capital from external investors, though the exact nature of any potential support remains unclear, Reuters reported this month.
Reuters was unable to independently establish details about AirAsia's financial picture.
Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air told the government they would only take over AirAsia's operations on a large scale if they could also assume its aircraft leases, one of the people said, as absorbing its routes and passenger volumes without the aircraft would be far more difficult.
Malaysia Airlines and Batik Air have both expressed to the government their willingness to expand organically to absorb AirAsia's routes and passengers rather than acquire its whole business, the people said.
AirAsia has said it commands about 40 per cent of Malaysia's overall aviation market and 60 per cent of domestic flying, making its financial challenges a significant concern for the government, the people interviewed by Reuters said.
Farouk Kamal, deputy group CEO of AirAsia Group, said in a statement that the airline does not comment on operational or financial speculation or unannounced corporate arrangements.
"All material updates regarding our business and fleet strategy are disclosed transparently through official exchange filings and corporate announcements at the appropriate time," he told Reuters.
"We also wish to reiterate that AirAsia remains focused on maintaining business continuity and stable operations across all its markets and we continue to see strong underlying demand across our network. We are also working closely with our stakeholders to manage our financial and operational requirements."
Malaysia Airports Holdings said it regularly engaged with all airline partners as part of normal network and route development, including on "potential capacity and route opportunities where there are gaps in the market or unmet demand." It declined to comment on AirAsia's financial outlook.
Malaysia's finance ministry, Batik Air and Malaysia Airlines declined to comment.

Also read:

AirAsia halts direct flights between Singapore and Jakarta

AirAsia launches first codeshare with Turkey's Pegasus Airlines

AIRASIA SEEKS FRESH CAPITAL AirAsia, which had current liabilities of RM18.4 billion (US$4.55 billion) as of Jun 30, owes Malaysia Airports Holdings at least RM500 million, the people and two others said, for services including landing and parking fees.
The airport operator has already granted the carrier repayment extensions, two of them said. They all declined to be identified because the discussions were private.
Malaysia Airports Holdings declined to comment on specific queries from Reuters, saying it did not discuss commercial arrangements with airline partners as a matter of practice. AirAsia did not address queries on whether it owed money to Malaysia Airports Holdings but said it had a strong and constructive relationship with key partners, including Malaysia Airports Holdings Chief Airports Officer Bryan Thompson and his team.
AirAsia said this month it was advancing discussions with financial institutions, targeting up to US$1 billion from international debt markets plus RM700 million in local credit facilities, primarily to restructure its debt.
Two of the people with knowledge of the matter estimated the airline required at least US$3 billion of fresh capital to address its financial position.
In response, AirAsia said its financing targets were sufficient to meet its requirements. The airline had cash and bank balances of RM954 million as of Jun 30.
AirAsia reported a net loss of RM831 million for the second quarter ended Jun 30, hit by rising jet fuel costs and heavy foreign-exchange losses of RM331 million.
The carrier has been restructuring aggressively, cutting underperforming routes, returning 25 older aircraft to lessors and renegotiating contracts with vendors to reduce costs.
Reuters reported this month that the finance ministry had hired Alton Aviation Consultancy to assess AirAsia's funding needs as it weighs whether to provide support given the airline's role as a major employer and provider of affordable air connectivity across the region.
The finance ministry declined to comment, while Alton did not respond to a request for comment.

Source: Reuters/bg

items.title: US court accepts airBaltic Chapter 11 filing, Latvian prime minister says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A U.S. court judge has accepted Latvian carrier airBaltic's request to enter Chapter 11 under the U.S. bankruptcy code and restructure its debt, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said on Wednesday.
items.body:
A U.S. court judge has accepted Latvian carrier airBaltic's request to enter Chapter 11 under the U.S. bankruptcy code and restructure its debt, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said on Wednesday.
"This means that airBaltic will be able to: immediately access financing; begin the restructuring process; review obligations to creditors. Work continues," Kulbergs said in a post on social media X.
The airline did not immediately reply to a request for comment.
AirBaltic, majority-owned by the Latvian government, [USN:L6N4560BF TEXT:"voluntarily filed"] for protection under Chapter 11 on Monday as it seeks to cut its debt pile after the Iran war increased financial pressure.
The company has said it secured a commitment for €350 million ($404.1 million) in financing from certain lenders, subject to court approval.
In the coming months, airBaltic is expected to negotiate with bondholders, aircraft lessors and other creditors as it works toward a formal reorganisation plan, which will require separate court approval before the company can exit Chapter 11.
The airline has said it aims to complete the process by around June 2027, with a [USN:L6N456122 TEXT:"reduced fleet"] and lower operating costs as part of its longer-term business plan.
($1 = 0.8661 euros)

items.title: WH Smith expects annual profit at lower end of forecast
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: British retailer WH Smith said on Wednesday it expects annual profit at the lower end of its earlier forecast range, as margins were squeezed by inflation turbo-charged by the Iran war and higher promotional activity.
items.body:
British retailer WH Smith (SMWH.L) said on Wednesday it expects annual profit at the lower end of its earlier forecast range, as margins were squeezed by inflation turbo-charged by the Iran war and higher promotional activity.
The company is reviewing its North American operations and shutting underperforming stores in a turnaround effort after cutting its profit forecast [USN:L6N42I0CU TEXT:"twice in two months"] and raising capital earlier this year as the war hit travel and passenger spending.
WH Smith, which sells everything from books to travel accessories and confectionery, expects headline pre-tax profit of about £75 million ($101 million) for the year ended August 31, compared with its earlier view of between £75 million and £90 million.
Its like-for-like sales in North America fell 3% in the fourth quarter, reflecting lower passenger volumes and softer demand, while sales in the UK grew 4%.
($1 = 0.7418 pounds)

items.title: 米ロサンゼルスでNBCヘリが墜落、3人死亡　事故現場取材中
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
NBCロサンゼルスは15日、ロサンゼルスのチャッツワース地区で同局のニュースヘリコプターが同日夜に墜落し、3人が死亡、1人が負傷したと報じた。

ロサンゼルス消防局によると、墜落現場で確認された4人のうち、3人は死亡、1人は容体が不明のまま地元の病院へ搬送された。

NBCのキャスターは、墜落したヘリコプターに何人が搭乗していたかには言及しなかった。

消防局によると、国家運輸安全委員会（NTSB）と連邦航空局（FAA）が墜落事故の調査を行うという。

ヘリコプターが墜落したチャッツワース地区ではこの日、バスと乗用車の衝突事故が起きていた。この衝突事故で少なくとも2人が死亡した。

複数のメディア報道によると、NBCのヘリコプターが墜落した際、衝突事故の取材のために数機の報道用ヘリコプターが現場付近に飛来していた。

米コムキャスト傘下のNBCとロサンゼルス消防局は、詳細に関する問い合わせに直ちには応じていない。

A rescuer works at a command post at Trisakti port on Sep 15, 2026, as the search and rescue operation continues after the Virgo Transport 8 ferry capsized in the Java Sea while sailing from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan. (Photo: Reuters/Stringer)

FAST

BANJARMASIN, Indonesia: Desperation and frustration are growing among families of the 129 people still missing following the weekend capsizing of a ship in Indonesia's Java Sea, as persistent heavy seas and bad weather continue to restrict search-and-rescue operations .
The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 243 people on a 20-hour voyage from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan when it capsized in bad weather early on Sunday (Sep 13).
On Wednesday, the official death toll stood at six people , with 108 rescued and 129 unaccounted for, tallies that have not changed since Sunday.
"I hope we would use our advanced military equipment, we buy them to help people, right? Or else what for? For war? We likely will not go to war,"  said 37-year-old Fauzi, who has been waiting for news of seven family members, including his mother, who were on the ship.

Fauzi, who goes by one name, said that after four days of waiting at the rescue command centre in Banjarmasin for promised updates about the search, his hopes have begun to fade.
"We do not hope much but what we need is certainty," he said.
The Coast Guard and Navy have been unable to launch underwater search-and-rescue operations because of waves of up to 2.5m and strong winds near the capsized vessel, I Putu Sudayana, the head of Banjarmasin's rescue agency, told Reuters.
On Wednesday, six ships were deployed for a surface search, Putu said, along with helicopters and aircraft.
Maria Dethan, 21, has stayed in the command centre since it was set up, anxiously waiting for news of her brother Samuel. 
"Every time I am about to eat, I always remember my brother because I believe he has been starving for days," she told Reuters, saying she needed some certainty from authorities. 
"I hope there will be clear information about my brother today," she said.

items.title: Caute in attesa decisione Fed, greggio in calo
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: I mercati azionari asiatici sono cauti, sostenuti dalla tregua nel massiccio sell-off obbligazionario globale e dal calo dei prezzi del greggio, elementi che hanno contribuito a placare i timori in vista della decisione della Federal Reserve di oggi.
items.body:
I mercati azionari asiatici sono cauti, sostenuti dalla tregua nel massiccio sell-off obbligazionario globale e dal calo dei prezzi del greggio, elementi che hanno contribuito a placare i timori in vista della decisione della Federal Reserve di oggi.
** L’indice più ampio MSCI relativo ai titoli dell’Asia-Pacifico escluso il Giappone (.MISX00000PUS) cede l'1,2% in chiusura di seduta, nonostante i rialzi dei titoli coreani (.KS11) e di quelli taiwanesi (.TWII) . Il Nikkei sale dello 0,3%, mentre i futures e-mini sull’S&P 500 registrano un rialzo dello 0,23%.
** Sul fronte obbligazionario, il rendimento dei titoli del Treasury a 10 anni rimane stabile al 4,9938% dopo aver sfiorato la soglia del 5%, superata ieri per la prima volta da tre anni. Nel corso della giornata la Fed comunicherà la propria decisione di politica monetaria, a cui farà seguito la conferenza stampa del presidente Kevin Warsh.
** Gli operatori ritengono che una stretta da parte della Federal Reserve sia quasi certa, scontando una probabilità implicita del 93% di un rialzo di 25 punti base, in netto aumento rispetto al 61,2% di una settimana fa.
** I prezzi del greggio arretrano nelle contrattazioni asiatiche, con i futures sul Brent in ribasso dello 0,65% a 108,04 dollari il barile, dopo il balzo del 2,9% di ieri, quando fonti del settore marittimo avevano riferito che le operazioni di carico del greggio presso l’hub di esportazione saudita di Yanbu, sul Mar Rosso, erano state sospese e che Riyadh aveva annullato alcune consegne di carico ai clienti europei.

items.title: 債券と株価の同時下落に留意､日銀利上げは｢織り込み済み｣-地銀協会長
items.author: Bloomberg
items.creator: Bloomberg
items.summary: （ブルームバーグ）：
items.body:
（ブルームバーグ）： 全国地方銀行協会の八木稔会長（静岡銀行頭取）は16日の会見で、国内で金利上昇（債券価格は下落）と株価の下落が同時に起きている市場環境に「留意が必要だ」と述べた。

国内では長期金利が30年ぶりに3%に達した。低利下で購入した国債の含み損を抱える地銀では、株の含み益で運用全体の成績を補っている銀行もあり、八木氏は「債券と株の逆相関が崩れているのは留意が必要だ」と語った。日経平均株価は6月に史上最高値を更新した後、上値が重い展開となっている。

日本銀行が17－18日に開く金融政策決定会合で追加の利上げを決めるとの公算が大きい。八木氏は「織り込みが進んでおり金融市場への影響は限定的だろう」と述べた。

住宅価格が高騰する中、金融庁は返済までの期間が50年といった超長期の住宅ローン商品への監視を強化している。八木氏は、超長期の住宅ローンについて「十分な説明をし返済能力を踏まえて提供している」との認識を示した。

items.title: El regulador de datos español informa sobre un acceso indebido relacionado con un agente de IA
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos dijo que había recibido la primera notificación de una violación de la seguridad de datos personales presuntamente llevada a cabo por un agente de inteligencia artificial, un caso que apunta a que los sistemas autónomos están empezando a desempeñar un papel directo en los ciberataques.
items.body:
La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos dijo que había recibido la primera notificación de una violación de la seguridad de datos personales presuntamente llevada a cabo por un agente de inteligencia artificial, un caso que apunta a que los sistemas autónomos están empezando a desempeñar un papel directo en los ciberataques.
La Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) dijo el lunes en una entrada de su blog que el incidente se produjo cuando un agente de IA utilizó un gran modelo de lenguaje muy conocido para identificar vulnerabilidades, acceder a un sistema y, posteriormente, modificar datos personales y acceder a facturas.
La agencia señaló que la supuesta vulneración le fue comunicada por la organización afectada y que la información sigue siendo objeto de análisis, y añadió que el uso de un modelo concreto de IA no significaba que ni el modelo en sí ni la infraestructura de su proveedor se hubieran visto comprometidos, ni que la tecnología se hubiera desarrollado con fines maliciosos.
La AEPD no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios de Reuters, ni identificó el modelo extenso de lenguaje ni la organización afectada por la violación de la seguridad de los datos.
La agencia señaló que el caso era relevante porque, al parecer, un tercero utilizó un agente de IA para llevar a cabo varias fases de un ataque con una intervención humana limitada, lo que pone de relieve el papel cada vez más importante de los sistemas autónomos en los incidentes de ciberseguridad.
El incidente se produce en un momento en que los reguladores y las autoridades de ciberseguridad de Estados Unidos y Europa están intensificando el escrutinio de los riesgos que plantean los sistemas de IA, cada vez más capaces, a pesar de que las empresas están adoptando esta tecnología a un ritmo vertiginoso.
PRIORIZAR LA SEGURIDAD PÚBLICA España [USN:L6N41Q0G7 TEXT:"se ha posicionado"] como uno de los defensores más activos de Europa de un modelo de "IA confiable" que proteja la privacidad, la democracia, a los menores y la seguridad pública, en lugar de dar prioridad a la rapidez o al beneficio de la industria tecnológica.
Aunque un solo caso no basta para establecer una tendencia más amplia, la notificación indica que los ataques asistidos por IA podrían estar dejando atrás la etapa teórica y comenzando a afectar al tratamiento de datos personales en el mundo real, añadió la AEPD.
Según la notificación presentada por la organización afectada, el agente logró acceder al sistema antes de buscar de forma autónoma puntos débiles en la aplicación. Tras identificar una vulnerabilidad, fue capaz de alterar información personal y consultar registros de facturación.
El organismo regulador español no ha indicado cuándo finalizará la investigación de la infracción notificada.
La agencia señaló que la IA no crea nuevas amenazas. Sin embargo, aumenta la velocidad, la escala y la adaptabilidad de las técnicas maliciosas existentes, lo que reduce el tiempo disponible para detectarlas y contenerlas.
Los responsables del tratamiento, los encargados del tratamiento y los delegados de protección de datos deben prepararse para un escenario en el que la velocidad de los ataques seguirá aumentando, añadió la agencia.

items.title: Francia respaldaría a Knot para dirigir el BCE y quiere el puesto de economista jefe
items.author: Michel Rose, Balazs Koranyi
items.creator: Michel Rose, Balazs Koranyi
items.summary: Francia respaldaría al neerlandés Klaas Knot para suceder a Christine Lagarde al frente del Banco Central Europeo, siempre y cuando el influyente puesto de economista jefe del BCE recayera en un candidato francés, han informado a Reuters fuentes cercanas.
items.body:
Francia respaldaría al neerlandés Klaas Knot para suceder a Christine Lagarde al frente del Banco Central Europeo, siempre y cuando el influyente puesto de economista jefe del BCE recayera en un candidato francés, han informado a Reuters fuentes cercanas.
La propuesta informal cuenta con el apoyo del presidente francés, Emmanuel Macron, según las fuentes. Sin embargo, es probable que se enfrente a una fuerte resistencia por parte de Alemania, lo que prepararía el terreno para un tira y afloja político de alto riesgo entre los pesos pesados políticos y económicos de la eurozona.
La oficina de Macron no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios, mientras que Knot se negó a hacer declaraciones. El Ministerio de Hacienda neerlandés no estuvo disponible de inmediato para hacer comentarios.
El BCE se negó a hacer comentarios.
La carrera por la sucesión ha cobrado impulso en las últimas semanas, ante especulaciones de que tanto Lagarde como su compañera en el Comité Ejecutivo, Isabel Schnabel, podrían dimitir antes de que expiren sus mandatos a finales de 2027, lo que aceleraría una reorganización en la cúpula del BCE.
La presidencia del BCE y otros cinco miembros del Comité Ejecutivo son nombrados por consenso entre los líderes de los 21 países de la eurozona, y las tres economías más grandes —Alemania, Francia e Italia— cuentan con una representación permanente de facto.
Una salida anticipada de Lagarde, de nacionalidad francesa, y de la alemana Schnabel aceleraría las decisiones que deben tomarse el año que viene y crearía las condiciones para alcanzar un amplio acuerdo que permita cubrir sus puestos y el del economista jefe, Philip Lane, cuyo mandato expira en mayo.
FRANCIA APOYA A KNOT FRENTE A DE COS Según el plan, Knot —que dirigió el banco central neerlandés de 2011 a 2025— asumiría la presidencia con el respaldo de Francia, según las fuentes, que hablaron bajo condición de anonimato porque dichas negociaciones son privadas y la propuesta sigue siendo informal.
Los participantes en el mercado consideran a Knot un pragmático, con una inclinación natural hacia una política monetaria más restrictiva, pero lo suficientemente flexible como para cambiar de rumbo según lo dicten los datos económicos.
"Es un 'halcón' (partidario de un endurecimiento monetario), pero de forma inteligente", dijo un representante francés sobre Knot.
El exgobernador del Banco de España Pablo Hernández de Cos, a quien se consideraba un voto oscilante en el Consejo de Gobierno encargado de fijar las tasas de interés, se perfila como el principal rival de Knot.
Sin embargo, dado que De Cos procede del sur de Europa, su nombramiento implicaría casi con toda seguridad que uno de los países "frugales" del norte de la zona euro asumiera el cargo de economista jefe para preservar el equilibrio de poder.
COMPETENCIA POR EL CARGO DE ECONOMISTA JEFE A cambio de respaldar a Knot, Francia quiere para sí el puesto de economista jefe —elegido por el presidente del BCE de entre los miembros del Comité Ejecutivo—, según las fuentes.
Identificaron a la vicegobernadora del Banco de Francia, Agnès Benassy-Quere, y a Laurence Boone, execonomista jefe de la OCDE y exministra adjunta de Asuntos Europeos en un anterior Gobierno de Macron, como nombres que figuran en la lista de candidatos de París.
Hélène Rey, que actualmente trabaja en el Banco de Pagos Internacionales, es otro nombre que ha barajado París, según las fuentes.
El nombramiento de cualquiera de ellas contribuiría en cierta medida a preservar el equilibrio de género en el consejo del BCE, donde Lagarde y Schnabel son actualmente las únicas mujeres.
Sin embargo, esta maniobra corre el riesgo de provocar una reacción inmediata por parte de Berlín. Aunque la propuesta dejaría a Alemania con el puesto que dejará vacante Schnabel y su cartera de operaciones de mercado, los responsables alemanes también tienen la mirada puesta en el cargo de economista jefe, considerado por muchos como el segundo puesto más influyente del consejo.
Los crecientes problemas de deuda de Francia han hecho que París esté más decidido que nunca a mantener un control firme sobre las riendas de la política monetaria de la zona euro. Alemania, menos endeudada y con una política económica más ortodoxa, sigue mostrándose recelosa ante cualquier flexibilización del compromiso del BCE con la estabilidad de precios.
LAGARDE HA DECLARADO QUE PERMANECERÁ EN EL CARGO HASTA 2027 Lagarde ha manifestado públicamente su interés en defender la integración europea de cara a las elecciones presidenciales del próximo año en Francia, donde la líder euroescéptica de extrema derecha, Marine Le Pen, goza de un gran apoyo en las encuestas.
Dimitir antes de las elecciones de mayo garantizaría a Macron una influencia decisiva a la hora de elegir al sucesor de Lagarde antes de que él abandone el cargo.
Lagarde no ha desmentido los rumores sobre una salida anticipada, limitándose a decir: "No me veréis marcharme antes de 2027". Los medios de comunicación la han relacionado con frecuencia con la dirección del Foro Económico Mundial.
Schnabel no ha hecho comentarios sobre una noticia publicada por el diario alemán Handelsblatt según la cual estaría en conversaciones para ocupar un alto cargo en el Fondo Monetario Internacional.
El mandato de ocho años de Lagarde concluye formalmente a finales de octubre de 2027, mientras que el de Schnabel finaliza dos meses después.

HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee unveiled the city's first five-year plan on Wednesday (Sep 16), aiming to boost residents' livelihoods and cement its position as a global financial hub, while beefing up technology ties with the mainland.
The sweeping plan, which follows two months of government consultations with lawmakers and residents, spans areas from the economy and investment to land, homes, jobs, education and health.
The plan envisages speeding development of the 30,000ha Northern Metropolis, near the mainland China border, as a new growth engine, bolstering technological links and ties with the mainland to add jobs and homes.
When complete, Lee said, it would be ideal for living, work and travel, "further boosting Hong Kong’s overall competitiveness and momentum for sustainable development".

The strategy comes after Beijing approved a national five-year plan in March for the years to 2030, in China's latest typical exercise laying out an official road map for social and economic development.
The Hong Kong plan's five major objectives include solidifying its financial, maritime and trade areas, accelerating efforts in information and technology and strengthening its role as a global offshore renminbi hub.
Hong Kong will act as a "super connector" and integrate with China's Greater Bay Area, Lee said.
"We will expedite the alignment with key national strategies in technology," he said.
The focus would be on areas ranging from lifestyle and healthcare to AI and robotics, microelectronics, new energy, advanced manufacturing and new materials, he added.
It will also strengthen efforts to develop itself into a centre for international legal and dispute resolution services, Lee added.
 

Related:

Hong Kong's five-year plan to retain capitalism, uphold ‘one country, two systems’ principle

NORTHERN METROPOLIS TO EASE HOUSING SHORTAGE The government first unveiled plans for the Northern Metropolis in 2021, aiming to provide homes for about 2.5 million people to alleviate a chronic shortage of housing, and establish a new business district.
It also includes plans for three university campus sites.
Authorities said the area will add about 650,000 jobs once fully developed.
A densely packed hub of 7.5 million, the former British colony has grappled with post-COVID pandemic malaise and a falling property market - long a mainstay of public revenues from land sales income.
Lee, a former policeman and Hong Kong security chief, took over its leadership in 2022, in the aftermath of COVID and mass anti-government protests in 2019 that led Beijing to impose a sweeping National Security Law the following year.
While Lee has spearheaded an economic recovery, his administration has also faced pressure from last November's Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po that killed 168 and made thousands homeless in the deadliest fire in decades.

FAST

Sept 16 : Independent phone and laptop makers are redesigning products, testing incoming chips for fakes and passing on costs as a memory shortage they expect to last through 2027 squeezes the lower end of the device market.
Availability, not price, is the binding constraint, executives at three companies said.
"If you don't have allocation, you're out of the game anyhow," said Raymond van Eck, chief executive of Dutch repairable-phone maker Fairphone.
Memory maker SK Hynix's CEO in July said 2027 would be "the worst year in the industry's history from the supply perspective," with demand outstripping capacity beyond 2030.

Counterpoint Research forecast in June that smartphone shipments would fall 13.9 per cent this year to 1.08 billion units, the steepest annual decline on record, as memory costs make entry-level phones uneconomical to build.
THE RALLY SLOWS, THE SHORTAGE DOESN'T
TrendForce expects conventional volatile memory (DRAM) contract prices up 13-18 per cent this quarter, against 93-98 per cent in the first.
Jolla, a Finnish handset maker founded by former Nokia engineers, said its combined storage and DRAM package rose to a peak at the end of March and has held since, confounding spring forecasts of a doubling by autumn.
"We are very happy for that, of course, for the time being," said Chief Executive Sami Pienimäki, who expects supply to normalise only from 2028.
The scale of the mismatch became clear late last year, said Nirav Patel, chief executive of U.S. repairable-laptop maker Framework, prompting "everyone trying to grab as much supply, as much inventory as they could, as quickly as they could", which deepened the shortage.
Unable to afford a stockpile, Framework places non-cancellable orders well ahead without knowing final price, timing or volume.
DESIGNING FOR SCARCITY
Jolla designed two motherboard variants so it can swap the combined package for discrete chips. Framework made memory modular from the start; customers now fit memory salvaged from older machines.
Jolla stress-tests samples from every batch it receives, checking the chips are new rather than refurbished parts resold as first-hand. Where prices spike, Pienimäki said, sellers follow.
Memory can account for almost 60 per cent of the bill of materials on handsets priced around $400, van Eck said. Each firm passes that on differently: Framework reprices quickly as costs land, Jolla added a paid memory upgrade, and Fairphone has not raised prices at all.

Source: Reuters

Memory can account for almost 60% of the bill of materials on handsets priced around $400, van Eck said. Each firm passes that on differently: Framework reprices quickly as costs land, Jolla added a paid memory upgrade, and Fairphone has not raised prices at all.
items.raw_description: Independent phone and laptop makers are redesigning products, testing incoming chips for fakes and passing on costs as a memory shortage they expect to last through 2027 squeezes the lower end of the device market.

items.title: Ukraine war drives European demand for bigger, cheaper missile arsenals
items.author: Maria Rugamer, Michael Kahn, Supantha Mukherjee
items.creator: Maria Rugamer, Michael Kahn, Supantha Mukherjee
items.summary: European militaries are increasingly exploring cheaper missiles and interceptors after conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East exposed the limits of small inventories of high-end weapons.
items.body:
European militaries are increasingly exploring cheaper missiles and interceptors after conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East exposed the limits of small inventories of high-end weapons.
Along Europe's eastern flank, Russia's daily drone and missile attacks on Ukraine have highlighted a lesson often overlooked in peacetime procurement planning: modern conflicts can consume weapons faster than many countries can replace them.
"If you think you have enough cruise missiles in your inventory, you probably don't," said Douglas Barrie of the International Institute for Strategic Studies.
Analysts say Europe's defence sector spent years focused on small production runs of sophisticated weapons rather than wartime-scale manufacturing, leaving governments now racing to seek lower-cost systems that can be fielded in greater numbers alongside advanced weapons from companies such as Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , MBDA and Rheinmetall (RHMG.DE) .
Industry executives say the challenge is no longer missile design but building the manufacturing capacity needed to sustain a modern conflict.
"Big wars are fought with numbers, not wonder weapons," said Stockholm International Peace Research Institute researcher Markus Schiller.
A new generation of defence startups says it can help meet the demand by developing cheaper missiles and interceptors designed for large-scale production.
The Netherlands in June ordered 700 Ruta Block 2 cruise missiles from European startup Destinus for Ukraine in a €250 million ($288 million) deal, while Britain's Ministry of Defence awarded initial Skyhammer interceptor contracts to Cambridge Aerospace.
"Given how the battlefield has evolved since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, developing low-cost but effective weapons systems is important," the Estonian Defence Forces told Reuters.
THE ARITHMETIC OF MODERN WAR Ukraine has already built a layered response, downing many of the thousands of long-range drones Russia launches each month with mounted machine guns, interceptor drones and electronic warfare to preserve more advanced interceptors for higher-end threats.
Steven Barrett, chief executive of Cambridge Aerospace, said Russia could launch up to 900 Shahed-type drones in a single night. Attempting to defeat them with traditional interceptors, as the U.S. has at times done in the Middle East, "would cost billions of dollars per night ... which is just impossible for any of our allies to sustain," he said.
Andreas Bappert, chief technology officer of missile company Frankenburg, said future systems must reduce the cost of a successful interception from as much as €20 million to around €1 million to €2 million.
Ukrainian startup Fire Point says it aims to build a ballistic-missile interceptor for less than €1 million, roughly one-quarter to one-sixth the cost of a U.S.-made Patriot air-defence interceptor.
Lockheed Martin this year unveiled a lower-cost Patriot missile. But even at less than half the cost of a Patriot PAC-3, it would remain above startup targets and is not expected to enter production until 2028.
Unlike the PAC-3, which is designed to defeat ballistic missiles and advanced aircraft, many of the emerging low-cost systems are focused primarily on drones, cruise missiles or other lower-end threats. Industry executives and analysts say they are intended to complement rather than replace high-end air-defence systems.
CAN EUROPE BUILD ENOUGH? Investors are increasingly backing emerging missile makers as they seek to scale production. Cambridge Aerospace raised $300 million last month to expand production, while Destinus is pursuing additional funding ahead of a planned IPO.
"The challenge for Europe is not that the technology does not exist," Destinus founder Mikhail Kokorich told Reuters. "The bigger challenge is industrial capacity, or the ability to produce, qualify and replenish systems on the scale required by modern conflicts."
Cambridge Aerospace is investing heavily to secure rocket motors and other critical components while incorporating commercial technologies such as automotive radar chips.
Fire Point uses a network of manufacturing partners, while Destinus has plugged into Rheinmetall's industrial base through a joint venture announced earlier this year.
Cambridge Aerospace aims to produce 2,500 interceptors a month by the end of the first quarter next year, while Frankenburg is targeting output of up to 100 missiles a day and 1,500 missiles in 2026.
Industry executives say scaling production depends not only on funding but also on securing components, obtaining approvals and expanding manufacturing processes.
Fire Point hopes to demonstrate a successful ballistic-missile interception by mid-2027, compressing what Chief Executive Iryna Terekh said would otherwise be a decades-long process into a few years.
Frankenburg Chief Executive Kusti Salm said manufacturing capacity itself could become a deterrent if adversaries concluded Europe could rapidly replace missiles consumed in combat.
"If the enemy knows that we can produce en masse ... the equation tells him, I'm not going to reach my objectives," he told Reuters.
($1 = 0.8671 euros)
items.raw_description: European militaries are increasingly exploring cheaper missiles and interceptors after conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East exposed the limits of small inventories of high-end weapons.

items.title: Una encuesta revela más confianza en las instituciones globales y menos apoyo al liderazgo de EEUU
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: Una nueva encuesta realizada a más de 35.000 personas de todo el mundo revela un apoyo continuado a la cooperación global y una confianza creciente en las instituciones internacionales, aunque también una menor aceptación de que Estados Unidos o China asuman roles de liderazgo. De hecho, muchos consideran que ambos países suponen una amenaza.
items.body:
Una nueva encuesta realizada a más de 35.000 personas de todo el mundo revela un apoyo continuado a la cooperación global y una confianza creciente en las instituciones internacionales, aunque también una menor aceptación de que Estados Unidos o China asuman roles de liderazgo. De hecho, muchos consideran que ambos países suponen una amenaza.
La encuesta, encargada por la Fundación Rockefeller y realizada en 34 países entre el 21 de julio y el 5 de agosto, reflejó una visión pesimista de la evolución económica y los retos de seguridad, y casi el 70% afirmó que el mundo había empeorado durante el último año.
Solo el 38% de los encuestados consideraba que la economía de su país mejoraría en los próximos cinco años, con un descenso pronunciado del optimismo en dos de las mayores economías. El optimismo cayó 26 puntos porcentuales en India, hasta el 50%, y 16 puntos en China, hasta el 56%.
A pesar del pesimismo generalizado, el 57% de los encuestados dijo que los países deberían cooperar para resolver retos globales como la seguridad, aunque ello suponga transigir en algunos intereses nacionales. Esta cifra supone un aumento respecto al 55% registrado en la encuesta del año pasado.
La encuesta, publicada antes de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas que se celebrará la próxima semana en Nueva York, se realiza tras casi siete meses de guerra en Oriente Medio que han trastornado los mercados energéticos mundiales, frenado el crecimiento económico y avivado la inflación. A ello le precedió un año de agitación provocado por los aranceles generalizados impuestos por el presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, a las importaciones procedentes de casi todos los países.
Estados Unidos e Israel iniciaron su guerra contra Irán el 28 de febrero, a lo que siguió el posterior cierre por parte de Teherán del estrecho de Ormuz, por donde transitaba el 20% del petróleo mundial. El conflicto se ha extendido a otros países, entre ellos Líbano, Yemen y Arabia Saudita, lo que ha añadido más presión al alza sobre los precios del petróleo.
La encuesta reveló que los encuestados no se sentían cómodos con Estados Unidos ni con China como líderes mundiales, y el 61% apoyaba que los países colaboraran sin la participación de ninguna de las dos mayores economías del mundo.
Canadá fue el país que recibió el mayor nivel de aceptación para asumir un papel de liderazgo en los asuntos mundiales, con un 60%, seguido de Japón (58%) y Australia (55%). La Unión Europea y Reino Unido los seguían de cerca, con un 55% y un 54%, respectivamente, mientras que Naciones Unidas se situaba en el 52%.
Por el contrario, solo el 39% se sentía cómodo con que Estados Unidos asumiera un papel de liderazgo y el 37% con que lo hiciera China. Rusia fue valorada de forma aún más negativa, con solo un 26% de opiniones favorables.
Eric Pelofsky, vicepresidente de la Fundación Rockefeller, dijo que los resultados de la encuesta demostraban que el enfoque de las "potencias intermedias", defendido por el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, gozaba de una credibilidad real a nivel mundial. Carney también ha calificado la guerra en Oriente Medio como un fracaso del orden mundial.
"(Los resultados) reflejan una profunda erosión del liderazgo mundial" de Estados Unidos, dijo Pelofsky. "La gente está debatiendo soluciones a los problemas globales y ya no se pregunta qué opinan los estadounidenses. Es un varapalo".
Las opiniones diferían notablemente entre las economías en desarrollo y las avanzadas: el 53% de los países en desarrollo se sentía cómodo con China, frente al 23% de los países más ricos. Rusia presentaba una diferencia de 27 puntos y Estados Unidos, de 17 puntos. Esta pregunta no se formuló en 2025.
Las instituciones internacionales vieron mejorar sus resultados durante el último año. La confianza en la Organización Mundial de la Salud aumentó del 61% al 69%, mientras que la puntuación de la ONU subió del 58% al 62%.
El Banco Mundial, el Fondo Monetario Internacional y la Corte Penal Internacional, que obtuvieron calificaciones insuficientes en la encuesta del año pasado, registraron las mayores mejoras.
La confianza en el Banco Mundial subió del 46% al 55%, la del Fondo Monetario Internacional pasó del 43% al 51% y la de la CPI alcanzó el 54%, frente al 48% del año pasado. La Organización Mundial del Comercio obtuvo un 57%, frente al 50% anterior.
Excluyendo la valoración del propio país de los encuestados, el 42% consideraba a Rusia una amenaza importante, frente al 34% que señalaba a EEUU y al 30% que señalaba a China. Rusia fue el país mencionado con mayor frecuencia como motivo de preocupación en 14 países, registrándose los porcentajes más altos en Europa.
Estados Unidos fue considerado la mayor amenaza en 15 países, con los porcentajes más elevados en Indonesia (73%), Brasil (59%), México (58%) y Turquía (57%).

De hecho, muchos consideran que ambos países suponen una amenaza.

items.title: UK homebuilder Barratt Redrow cuts annual home completions target
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Barratt Redrow , Britain's largest homebuilder, trimmed its home completions target for fiscal 2027 on Wednesday, citing planning delays and fewer sales outlet openings.
items.body:
Barratt Redrow (BTRW.L) , Britain's largest homebuilder, trimmed its home completions target for fiscal 2027 on Wednesday, citing planning delays and fewer sales outlet openings.
"Whilst recent planning reforms should, in time, boost housing delivery, alone they will not be enough," Barratt Redrow said in a statement, urging the government to support demand, particularly for first-time buyers.
Barratt Redrow has been cutting its land spending and approval targets, anticipating higher costs from rising energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict, while homebuyers remain cautious ahead of October's budget.
The company reported adjusted pre-tax profit of £572.8 million for the year ended June 28, ahead of market expectations of £540.30 million, according to LSEG data, though down 7.1% from a year earlier as sales incentives and build cost inflation squeezed margins.
The company said it now expected to deliver between 17,500 and 17,900 homes in the year ending June 2027, down from earlier guidance of 17,700 to 18,200, and lowered its average sales outlet expectation to about 405 from 415.
items.raw_description: Barratt Redrow , Britain's largest homebuilder, trimmed its home completions target for fiscal 2027 on Wednesday, citing planning delays and fewer sales outlet openings.

items.title: Carney visita Europa para estrechar lazos ante el recrudecimiento de la guerra comercial con Trump
items.author: Maria Cheng, Julia Payne
items.creator: Maria Cheng, Julia Payne
items.summary: El primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, viajará a Estrasburgo el miércoles, convirtiéndose en el primer jefe de Gobierno extranjero en asistir al discurso sobre el Estado de la Unión de la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, en un momento en el que busca nuevas alianzas ante las repetidas amenazas del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, contra la soberanía de Canadá.
items.body:
El primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, viajará a Estrasburgo el miércoles, convirtiéndose en el primer jefe de Gobierno extranjero en asistir al discurso sobre el Estado de la Unión de la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, en un momento en el que busca nuevas alianzas ante las repetidas amenazas del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, contra la soberanía de Canadá.
Carney se dirigirá al Parlamento Europeo el jueves para exponer su visión de "una alianza única" entre Canadá y Europa.
Carney se ha comprometido a duplicar el comercio de Canadá con países distintos de Estados Unidos en la próxima década, en un momento en que el país se aleja de su vecino del sur en medio de una guerra comercial cada vez más encarnizada.
Siete diplomáticos de la UE en Canadá y Europa han declarado a Reuters que se están realizando esfuerzos activos para lograr una colaboración más profunda en materia de comercio, defensa y seguridad digital, pero que aún no se ha debatido a alto nivel ningún plan específico para una relación más integral entre Canadá y la UE.
Carney afirmó el martes que se iniciarían debates más detallados en la cumbre entre Canadá y la UE que se celebrará en Montreal a finales de octubre.
"Nuestra relación con la UE se ha vuelto cada vez más estrecha, especialmente durante el último año y medio", dijo a Reuters la ministra de Asuntos Exteriores canadiense, Anita Anand. "La UE destaca como una jurisdicción en la que no solo hay valores compartidos, sino también intereses económicos comunes".
La semana pasada, el Wall Street Journal informó de que Carney había sugerido a los líderes europeos que Canadá se convirtiera en "miembro asociado" de la UE.
Cuatro diplomáticos de la UE en Canadá afirmaron que cualquier tipo de adhesión de Canadá a la UE era imposible, señalando las limitaciones geográficas y las implicaciones jurídicas que conlleva la pertenencia a la Unión.
"Queremos reforzar la relación entre Canadá y la UE, pero, aunque ambos creemos en un orden mundial basado en normas, hay un océano que nos separa", dijo uno de los diplomáticos.
OBSTÁCULOS SIGNIFICATIVOS Siguen existiendo obstáculos significativos para impulsar el comercio. Mark Manger, profesor de economía política y asuntos globales en la Universidad de Toronto, señaló que los responsables de la UE se han sentido frustrados por la negativa de Canadá a abrir dos sectores que protege a un alto coste: las telecomunicaciones y el sector lácteo.
"Tendríamos que poner sobre la mesa algo que la UE quiera, pero, por el momento, ambos mercados están simplemente cerrados", señaló Manger. Aunque Canadá tiene un acuerdo comercial con la UE de 27 miembros, 10 países aún no lo han ratificado.
Anand Sundar, asesor especial del director del Consejo Europeo de Relaciones Exteriores, señaló que los responsables están trabajando en propuestas para establecer una relación única entre Canadá y la UE, similar a los acuerdos que la UE mantiene con otros Estados no miembros.
"La defensa es el ámbito en el que la dependencia de Europa y Canadá respecto a EEUU es más profunda, donde ambas partes se enfrentan a amenazas similares y para el que resulta más fácil conseguir el apoyo de la opinión pública", señaló Sundar. En diciembre, Canadá aceptó sumarse a una iniciativa europea, convirtiéndose así en el primer país no europeo en participar en la estrategia continental de adquisición de material de defensa.
Cuatro diplomáticos europeos señalaron que, aunque muchos de sus líderes se han mostrado en privado consternados por los ataques verbales de Trump contra Canadá, la mayoría se muestra reacia a respaldar públicamente el enfoque más agresivo de Carney en las negociaciones comerciales con EEUU, por temor a que el presidente pueda volverse entonces contra Europa.
El embajador designado de Canadá ante la UE, Jonathan Wilkinson, señaló que los responsables europeos han mantenido un estrecho contacto con el Gobierno de Carney y que existe un amplio apoyo tácito, basándose en el tamaño de la UE y su enfoque en cuestiones que ayudan a Canadá a hacer valer su soberanía, como la inteligencia artificial y los servicios digitales.
"No hemos pedido a los líderes europeos que se pronuncien y hagan una declaración de apoyo a Canadá, y no creo que lo necesitemos", dijo. "Podemos defendernos por nosotros mismos y encontrar nuevas formas de trabajar".

items.title: UK inflation hits 3.1% but data offers some relief for BoE
items.author: William Schomberg, Andy Bruce
items.creator: William Schomberg, Andy Bruce
items.summary: British inflation accelerated to a five-month high of 3.1% in August, but measures excluding surging energy prices held stable, official figures showed on Wednesday, a day before the Bank of England is expected to keep interest rates on hold.
items.body:
British inflation accelerated to a five-month high of 3.1% in August, but measures excluding surging energy prices held stable, official figures showed on Wednesday, a day before the [USN:L8N45318O TEXT:"Bank of England"] is expected to keep interest rates on hold.
The increase in the annual headline rate was in line with forecasts by economists polled by Reuters, who predicted it would be impacted by the resumption of conflict in the Gulf.
Further increases are likely in the coming months when domestic energy bills — which track global market prices with a lag — go up.
"Sharp price rises for petrol and diesel pushed inflation up again in August. Higher airfares, particularly for long-haul journeys, also contributed to the increase," Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the Office for National Statistics, said.
"Rising crude oil and petrol prices increased both the annual cost of raw materials and the price of goods leaving factories respectively."
The inflation pickup adds to the headaches of Prime Minister Andy Burnham and finance minister John Healey who have offered voters some support with the cost of living but whose options in a budget plan due on October 28 are limited by the weak state of the public finances.
"The war in the Middle East is impacting on inflation worldwide, not just here at home. In our bills, our weekly shop and at the petrol pumps," Healey said after the release of the inflation figures.
CORE AND SERVICES INFLATION LIKELY TO REASSURE BOE Despite the headline rate of annual inflation coming in higher than the central bank expected when it made its most recent forecasts in July, policymakers are likely to pay more attention to the underlying measures of price growth.
The ONS said its measure of core inflation — which excludes volatile items such as food as well as fuel — held at 2.6% for a fourth month in a row in August.
Inflation in Britain's services sector — something the BoE watches closely as it reflects wage growth and longer-term inflation pressures — was also unchanged at 3.4%.
"With limited evidence of second-round effects so far, we expect the MPC to hold rates tomorrow," Charlotte O'Leary, associate economist at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said.
ONS data [USN:L8N45708S TEXT:"published on Tuesday"] showed wage growth remained close to its weakest since 2020.
"However, mounting inflationary pressures, alongside resilient growth data, may eventually grant scope to raise rates without materially damaging the economy," O'Leary added.
INFLATION COULD PEAK AT 3.9%, GOLDMAN WARNS Sterling fell slightly after the inflation figures were published.
Investors see a roughly 20% chance of the BoE hiking rates by a quarter point on Thursday. However, there is a 75% chance that two rate hikes will take place before the end of 2026, reflecting concerns about the risk of the jump in energy costs pushing up prices more broadly.
Goldman Sachs said this week it expected Britain's headline inflation rate to peak at 3.9% in early 2027.
Britain's economy grew by the most among the Group of Seven nations in the first half of 2026, potentially adding to inflation pressure.
Producer price inflation, which measures manufacturers' costs and selling prices, looked more worrisome for the BoE in terms of longer-term inflation pressure.
Output prices rose by 3.7% in annual terms in August, above all forecasts after an upwardly revised 3.3% in July, the ONS said. Input prices rose by 6.1% while July's reading was revised up sharply to 5.8% from 4.9% previously.
items.raw_description: British inflation accelerated to a five-month high of 3.1% in August, but measures excluding surging energy prices held stable, official figures showed on Wednesday, a day before the Bank of England is expected to keep interest rates on hold.

items.title: ByteDance completes $290 million fundraising for AI drug unit after its spin-off, sources say
items.author: Kane Wu
items.creator: Kane Wu
items.summary: Chinese social media and internet company ByteDance has completed a $290 million fundraising for its AI drugmaking unit after spinning it off from the group, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Chinese social media and internet company ByteDance has completed a $290 million fundraising for its AI drugmaking unit after spinning it off from the group, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.
Shanghai-headquartered Anew Labs, which uses AI for drug discovery, has achieved a valuation of $1.5 billion after its inaugural external fundraising, said one of the sources.
The fundraising was led by HSG, formerly known as Sequoia China, IDG Capital and Hillhouse Investment, the sources said, adding that 5Y Capital was a co-lead investor.
Other investors included Gaorong Ventures, Primavera Venture Partners, Boyu Capital as well as strategic investor SBP Group and state-backed Shanghai Future Industries Fund, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity as the information is not public.
ByteDance and the investors did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
ByteDance spun off the AI drugmaker to better support its long-term development, as AI drug discovery follows a different industry logic and management approach than the group's core operations, said one of the sources.
ByteDance will maintain a 56% stake after the fundraising, said the second source.
items.raw_description: Chinese social media and internet company ByteDance has completed a $290 million fundraising for its AI drugmaking unit after spinning it off from the group, two people with knowledge of the matter said on Wednesday.

items.author: Bantirani Patro

Is the China-Pakistan arms nexus exporting authoritarianism? The case of the JF-17

Arms sales to non-democratic states by like-minded regimes are a subtle yet consequential tool of extending sway. The JF-17’s export pattern fits this description closely

Bantirani Patro
